items.title: Fifa president Infantino will stand for re-election
items.summary: Infantino is under pressure to resign after sell-off plan Uefa has led calls for president to quit The Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, has reiterated his desire to stand for re-election next year despite the continuing controversy surrounding his leadership. Infantino refused to answer questions about his future when asked by reporters at the Women’s Under-20 World Cup in Poland on Saturday. The 56-year-old Swiss is under severe pressure to resign after trying to sell stakes in Fifa tournaments, including the World Cup, to private investors.

items.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
items.summary: Fulham need a win, Tottenham show some spirit and Jack Grealish offers Everton much-needed energy With 25 minutes to go against Manchester United, the Everton supporters had something to roar about as Jack Grealish made his return after rejoining on loan. The attacking midfielder remains universally popular thanks to his desire to entertain, getting the hosts back on their feet by creating dangerous situations within seconds of his arrival. Everton were limited in the final third for long periods as Thierno Barry sat on the periphery.

items.title: Scottish Premiership: Celtic’s Yang completes fightback to see off St Mirren
items.summary: Rangers beat Motherwell 1-0 but lose Shankland to injury Kerjota’s late winner sees Hearts edge past Dundee Yang Hyun-jun scored the winner as Celtic came from behind to beat an impressive St Mirren side 2-1. St Mirren were heading for the top of the Premiership when Nikolas Agrafiotis netted from the spot midway through the first half. Liam Scales conceded the penalty with a handball but made amends when he headed home six minutes after the break.

items.title: ‘Exceptional performance’: Arteta hails fightback win and says best yet to come
items.summary: Manager delighted by reaction to Chelsea’s opener Alonso says his side must be ‘tighter’ Mikel Arteta warned that Arsenal are capable of hitting even greater heights after the Premier League champions sent a statement to their title rivals by fighting back from a goal down to beat Chelsea on Sunday. Arteta’s side were under pressure after conceding for the first time this season when Morgan Rogers struck early at the Emirates Stadium, but the response to the setback was outstanding. Kai Havertz equalised before conjuring a brilliant dummy for a rejuvenated Martin Ødegaard to make it 2-1, ensuring that Arsenal moved level on points with Manchester City at the top of the Premier League.

items.title: ‘No excuses’: Moyes says transfer troubles will not hurt Everton after United draw
items.summary: Manager praises team’s resilience after late equaliser ‘Everyone has to find a way of making it work’ David Moyes praised Everton’s resilient response to a troubled week after his side twice came from behind to salvage a point against Manchester United through Ainsley Maitland-Niles’s long-range strike. The deadline-day signing, who was introduced in the 77th minute after James Garner pulled up with cramp, preserved Everton’s unbeaten start to the season with a 25-yard effort in the 96th minute.

items.title: Jamie Vardy takes party to Burnley after signing deal with Championship strugglers
items.summary: Vardy a free agent after departing Cremonese Plans to play on despite burgeoning media career Jamie Vardy has returned to English football after signing for Burnley in the Championship as a free agent. Vardy, who will be 40 in January, has signed a contract until the end of the season, having spent last season at Cremonese in Italy. A return to Leicester, where he spent 13 years and was a Premier League champion in 2016 and an FA Cup winner in 2021, was mooted in the summer, only for Vardy to rule out a reunion.

items.title: ‘Reverse bucket list’: Arteta channels Wenger in defence of Arsenal window
items.summary: The champions’ manager echoed his illustrious predecessor and urged fans unhappy at the lack of a deadline-day arrival to see the bigger picture For many people connected to Arsenal, it has been a time to remember the old line from Arsène Wenger. “We live in a society of ‘news’,” the club’s former manager once said, and by that he meant new things – the shinier the better. Nowhere is the obsession more obvious than in the transfer market, when a club simply has to add new faces.

items.title: ‘The noise was unbelievable’: the referee’s view of Mexico v England at the World Cup

His assistants had turned the music down.

items.title: Chelsea hit bullseye with Morgan Rogers as Arsenal rue what might have been
items.summary: The Gunners will have a look at what they could have won when the former Villa man lines up against them, having made a flying start for Xabi Alonso’s team Chelsea thought they had little chance of signing Morgan Rogers at the start of the summer. Xabi Alonso and the club’s recruitment team had the England international as a priority target but a deal seemed unlikely. Chelsea had endured a disappointing season, missing out on European football after finishing 10th, and their expectation was that Rogers would leave Aston Villa for Arsenal.

items.title: Premier League paradox: midfielders are more and more expensive, yet more and more mediocre | Jonathan Liew
items.summary: Xabi Alonso’s side have scored seven and conceded five in two wins so far, a product of the squad’s constant churn Sign up for our free newsletter here Two Premier League games played for Chelsea under Xabi Alonso: two wins and seven goals scored. It’s the sort of start that would delight many new managers – only two other clubs can boast about a six-point start this Premier League season (albeit with Arsenal to play later on Monday). Points gained in this odd transitional phase, when almost nobody seems quite ready, could prove extremely valuable come the end of the season.

items.title: Måndag morgon: Och så var fönstret stängt
items.summary: Lund. Visst. Det kan hända att något fönster fortfarande är öppet så något kan hända men i stort så är det stängt nu och vi vet vad vi har att jobba med inför fortsättningen. Vi tar en titt på lagdel för lagdel. Ricardo Friedrich försvann ut. Hade såklart varit en ok andre- eller tredjemålvakt men det var inte bra för någon att han var kvar. Dessutom högst sannolikt dyr som handplockad av Rydström som en av seriens bästa målvakter. Svårt att veta alla turer men känns ändå märkligt att det inte gick att sälja.
